title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 47
paragraphs: When the Pythian prophetess had uttered this oracle, the Lydians had the prophecy written down and went away at once to Sardis. And when the others also who had been sent to the various shrines had returned with the answers of the Oracles, Croesus then unrolled the writings one by one and looked them over. At first none of them pleased him, but when he heard the answer from Delphi, he at once worshipped the god and accepted it, judging that the Oracle at Delphi was the only true one, because it had discovered what he himself had been doing. For when he had sent to the several Oracles his messengers to consult the gods, keeping the appointed day firmly in mind, he had contrived the following device: he thought of something that would be impossible to discover or even to imagine, and cutting up a tortoise and a lamb, he boiled them together himself in a cauldron of bronze, laying a cover of bronze over them.”
